description: Divisorial sheet loss has only three allowed types, and the quadratic resolvent rules out isolated support for a nonflat cubic defect; a smooth-axis exclusion is conditional on extension of the transverse three-torsion class.

independent_review.scope: No independent review is represented in this public record.

manuscript_coverage.coverage_rule: Complete coverage requires an exact LaTeX location for every program-relevant defining claim. A locator records where the current statement and evidence boundary appear; it is not a proof-review status.

members.statement: For a complex generic-degree-three Keller map, every target prime divisor has a retained unramified sheet and hence only the U1, U2, or B deleted-sheet type; a deleted three-cycle is impossible, and the generic monodromy is S3.
members.title: Cubic Keller Maps Have Only the U1, U2, and B Divisorial Types

members.statement: For the quadratic resolvent Q of a complex cubic Keller normalization, an isolated singularity cannot support a nonflat cubic defect; moreover, three-torsion in Cl(Q) is detected at the height-two singular primes.
members.title: A Cubic Defect Forces a Nonisolated Quadratic-Resolvent Singularity

members.statement: In the stated one-parameter smooth cubic-axis hypersurface model, when the transverse three-torsion class extends as a section of the relative three-torsion group scheme, its rank-one reflexive module is maximal Cohen-Macaulay and the associated cubic normalization is flat.
members.title: The Smooth Cubic-Axis Resolvent Model Is Flat
